To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the small molecule PES inhibits HSP70 family members and that PES-mediated HSP70 inhibition impairs protein clearance pathways in tumor cells.

HSP70 is a critical protein quality control factor in cancer cells and its inhibition with PES results in a loss of the two major cellular protein degradation pathways, the proteasome and the autophagy/lysosome systems.
PES-mediated disruption of the HSP70 chaperone system leads to an impairment of the autophagy and proteasome pathways, resulting in a build-up of misfolded and aggregated proteins in tumor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the HSP70 molecular machinery is regulated, and how it contributes to the development and survival of cancer cells.

the development and application of novel small-molecule HSP70 inhibitors as a potential approach to cancer therapeutics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HSP70 inhibitor PES is a potent inhibitor of HSP70 and that it has a significant impact on the proteasome and lysosome degradation pathways in tumor cells.
PES inhibits HSP70 family protein function, leading to the disruption of the HSP70-HSP90 chaperon system, which in turn results in the accumulation of misfolded and aggregated cellular proteins.

HSP70 inhibition by PES impairs the protein degradation pathways in cancer cells, leading to the accumulation of misfolded, aggregation-prone proteins and the loss of their function, thus contributing to the cell death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HSP70 inhibitor 2-phenyl-ethynesulfonamide ( PES ) is a novel inhibitor of HSP70 that inhibits both HSP70 and HSP70-HSP90 chaperones and causes the accumulation of proteins in detergent-insolubile cell fractions.
PES is a small molecule that inhibits the HSP70 chaperone and thereby causes an impairment in the two major protein quality control pathways, autophagy and the proteasomal pathway.
HSP70 inhibition by PES impairs protein degradation pathways, resulting in the accumulation of proteins in insoluble cell fractions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inhibition of HSPs by small molecules can have a significant impact on the protein degradation systems in cells, and this can lead to the accumulation of proteins and the disruption of cellular pathways.
HSP70 inhibition can have pleiotropic effects on protein quality control pathways in tumor cells.
HSP70 family molecular chaperones play a critical role in maintaining protein homeostasis in tumor cells.
